entries.sense_en: clever and quick to understand situations and people

synonyms.nuance: General and neutral; can mean good at school, tricks or ideas, not only practical judgment.
More formal; stresses sharp judgment, often in business or politics.
Clever in a tricky, often dishonest way; more negative than shrewd.
synonyms.example: a cunning plan to cheat them

entries.tip_ko: shrewd는 칭찬에 가깝지만 약간 '계산이 빠르다'는 느낌도 있습니다. 발음은 '슈루드'에 가깝습니다.

entries.sense_en: a big untidy pile of things

synonyms.nuance: The everyday word; can be neat or messy.
Neat and orderly, one flat thing on top of another.
A rounded heap, usually of earth, sand or snow.

entries.sense_en: a proud claim about yourself or your family, often not true

synonyms.nuance: More informal and more negative; the speaker sounds annoying.
synonyms.example: He likes to brag about his car.

synonyms.nuance: Usually about actions or things you display, not words.
synonyms.example: She was showing off her new ring.

synonyms.nuance: Neutral statement that something is true; no pride implied.
synonyms.example: his claim that he was innocent

entries.sense_en: a room, especially a private room in a palace or castle

synonyms.nuance: The ordinary everyday word for any room.
A large room for many people, or a corridor.

entries.sense_en: without success; the effort changed nothing

synonyms.nuance: Informal; also used when effort or money was wasted.
Formal adjective describing the attempt itself.
Describes a thing or action that cannot help at all; stronger and plainer.

entries.tip_ko: vain(허영심 있는)과 in vain(헛되이)은 뜻이 다릅니다.

entries.sense_en: a young unmarried woman

synonyms.nuance: Everyday modern word; covers children too.
Neutral, modern and polite for an adult.
synonyms.example: a young woman in a red coat

synonyms.nuance: Even more old-fashioned; now mostly jokey, as in 'damsel in distress'.

entries.sense_en: to cry and complain loudly about something sad

synonyms.nuance: Formal; expresses sorrow, often in words or poems, less noisy.
synonyms.example: lament the loss of a friend

synonyms.nuance: Today usually means complaining about a situation, not deep grief.
Grieve for someone who has died; serious and quiet.

entries.sense_en: funny in a strange or unusual way

synonyms.nuance: Everyday word for anything that makes you laugh.
Funny to look at, often without meaning to be.
Modern; odd in an interesting, likeable way, not necessarily funny.

entries.sense_en: walked with difficulty, with short uneven steps

synonyms.nuance: Walk unevenly because one leg is hurt; the most common word.
Walk slowly without lifting the feet, often from age or tiredness.
synonyms.example: shuffle to the kitchen in slippers

synonyms.nuance: Walk unsteadily, almost falling, e.g. drunk or hit.

entries.sense_en: an old greeting meaning 'good morning' or 'good day'

synonyms.nuance: The modern greeting, used only before noon.
Old-fashioned or formal in the US; still heard in Australia.

entries.sense_en: a girl or young woman (friendly, old or Scottish/northern English)

synonyms.nuance: Standard everyday word.
More literary and formal; lass is warm and homely.
Scottish, even more affectionate diminutive.

entries.sense_en: a small, ugly, mischievous creature from folk tales

synonyms.nuance: Usually uglier and more evil; common in fantasy stories.
Often beautiful or kind; small helpful elves in fairy tales.
A small naughty devil; also a naughty child.

entries.sense_en: to accept exactly what someone says or offers and act on it

synonyms.nuance: Accept an offer or invitation; lighter and more casual.
synonyms.example: I'll take you up on that coffee.

synonyms.nuance: Only thinking it is true; no action follows.

entries.sense_en: look! see this surprising thing

synonyms.nuance: Plain everyday call for attention.
Neutral adverb; lo and behold is now used humorously for surprises.

entries.sense_en: wind the thread onto a wheel or spool, again and again

synonyms.nuance: General word for turning something around a thing.
synonyms.example: wind the wool into a ball

synonyms.nuance: Make thread by twisting fibers, as on a spinning-wheel.
Turn round very fast; about movement, not thread.
synonyms.example: The leaves whirled in the wind.

entries.tip_ko: 여기서 away는 '계속해서'라는 뜻입니다 (work away, sing away).

entries.sense_en: shining with many small flashes of light

synonyms.nuance: Similar, but often lively and happy, like eyes or water.
Smooth and bright; steady shine, not small flashes.
Soft, clean shine, often of polished things.

entries.sense_en: a very small man

synonyms.nuance: Common in fairy tales for a small magical man.
synonyms.example: Snow White and the seven dwarfs

synonyms.nuance: Plain everyday phrase; manikin is rare and old.
synonyms.example: a little man with a beard

synonyms.nuance: Same origin, but now means a shop dummy for clothes.

entries.sense_en: to do what you promised

synonyms.nuance: Same meaning, a bit plainer; word stresses personal honor.
Finish what you started or planned, not only promises.

entries.sense_en: to make someone remember something

synonyms.nuance: The normal modern word.
Brings back memories, often pleasant or emotional.

entries.tip_ko: 오늘날 put in mind of는 '닮아서 연상시키다'(He puts me in mind of my father)로 주로 씁니다.

entries.sense_en: felt very sad and troubled

synonyms.nuance: Mainly for someone who has died, often shown publicly.
Everyday and much weaker.
synonyms.example: She was upset about the test.

synonyms.nuance: Literary verb or noun for deep sadness.

entries.sense_en: very much, in a painful way

synonyms.nuance: Neutral intensifier for feelings.
Informal; with need or want means very much.
Sad with anger or resentment.

entries.tip_ko: 오늘날엔 sorely missed(몹시 그리운), sorely needed처럼 굳은 표현으로 씁니다.

entries.sense_en: to free someone from a promise, duty or punishment

synonyms.nuance: Formal; free someone from a duty or a place.
Allow someone not to do a duty, usually small.
Stop holding or keeping someone; also 'fire from a job'.

entries.tip_ko: let off with a warning(경고로 봐주다)처럼 처벌에 자주 씁니다.

entries.sense_en: extra time allowed before something must be done or paid

synonyms.nuance: Extra time added to a deadline, common at school or work.
Something happens later; not necessarily allowed kindly.
A cancellation or delay of punishment; more dramatic.

entries.tip_ko: grace period(유예 기간)는 요금·대출에서 지금도 흔히 씁니다.

entries.sense_en: to make beer (for a feast)

synonyms.nuance: General word; brew is specific to beer, tea or coffee.
The chemical process itself, used for wine, kimchi, etc.
Leave tea or herbs in hot water; one step of brewing tea.

entries.sense_en: to laugh quietly, often to yourself

synonyms.nuance: Light, high, silly laugh, often of children or nervous people.
Unkind, half-hidden laugh at someone.
Loud harsh laugh, like a witch.

entries.sense_en: in a clever, secretive way, hiding what you know

synonyms.nuance: Clever and tricky, more negative and serious.
Teasing for fun, without any secret.
Skillfully deceiving to get what you want.

entries.sense_en: to take and hold firmly

synonyms.nuance: Quick and sudden, everyday word.
Hold very tightly, focus on the pressure.
Take suddenly and forcefully; also used for police taking things.

entries.match: made the best of his way off
entries.headword: make the best of one's way
entries.sense_en: went away as fast as he could

synonyms.nuance: Leave quickly; plain everyday phrase.
Run away from danger; serious and formal.
Leave quietly because you feel ashamed.

entries.tip_ko: make the best of(최대한 활용하다)와 헷갈리지 마세요.

entries.sense_en: (of a baby) made happy little cries of pleasure

synonyms.nuance: Soft, gentle happy sounds of a baby or dove.
synonyms.example: The baby cooed in her arms.

synonyms.nuance: Bubbly, throaty baby sounds.
Adult crowing: showing nasty pleasure at someone's failure.

entries.sense_en: laughed at and shouted rude things at someone

synonyms.nuance: Make fun of by copying or joking; can be quiet.
Light, often friendly fun.
Shout 'boo' in a crowd to show disapproval.

entries.tip_ko: jeer at someone 형태로 자주 씁니다.
